briefing.summary: April 1, 2025 is the eve of 'Liberation Day' — Trump's sweeping reciprocal tariff announcement scheduled for April 2. Markets closed Q1 with the S&P 500 down 4.27% for the quarter and 5.63% in March alone, closing at 5,580.94 on March 31. VIX jumped 15.8% to 21.65. Gold surged past $3,100 to all-time highs ($3,122.80). ISM Manufacturing PMI contracted to 49.0 from 50.3. The Fed held rates at 4.25-4.50% on March 19 with Powell warning tariffs could delay inflation progress. Auto tariffs of 25% announced March 26 already hammered GM (-7%) and Ford (-3%). Tesla plunged 36% in Q1 on DOGE backlash and boycotts. The market is bracing for tariff escalation but dramatically underestimates the scope — 10% baseline on ALL imports, 34% China (54% cumulative), 20% EU, 46% Vietnam, 25% Japan/S.Korea. This information asymmetry is the core edge. Defensive rotation into gold, utilities, healthcare, and domestic producers is the dominant theme. The S&P 500 will lose $5.83T in market value over the 4 days following the announcement — the steepest 4-day loss since the index was created.

sections.title: Geopolitics
sections.content: Trump's Liberation Day tariff announcement on April 2 dominates all geopolitical considerations. The market expects tariffs but dramatically underestimates the scope: 10% baseline on ALL imports (effective April 5), plus country-specific rates — 34% on China (54% total with existing 20%), 20% on EU, 46% on Vietnam, 32% on Taiwan, 25% on Japan and South Korea. Auto tariffs of 25% already announced March 26, effective April 3. European rearmament accelerating massively with EUR 800B+ ReArm Europe plan announced March 4 after Germany exempted defense from constitutional debt limits. This is the most sweeping tariff action since the Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act of 1930.

sections.title: Macro
sections.content: Fed held rates at 4.25-4.50% on March 19. Powell warned a 'good part' of higher inflation expectations comes from tariffs but still projected two rate cuts in 2025. ISM Manufacturing PMI dropped to 49.0 (contraction) from 50.3 in February, with respondents citing tariff uncertainty as the primary driver. S&P 500 closed Q1 at 5,580.94, down 4.27% for the quarter and 5.63% in March. VIX at 21.65, up 15.8% on March 31. Gold surged past $3,122.80, on track for strongest quarter since 1986. 10 of 11 S&P sectors ended March 31 in negative territory. Consumer spending moderating after strong H2 2024.

sections.title: Corporate
sections.content: Tesla plunged 36% in Q1 — worst quarter since 2022 — on DOGE backlash, boycotts, declining sales, and Musk's divided attention. GM stock dropped 7% on auto tariff announcement (March 26), with Bernstein estimating 79% EBIT decline. Nike faces existential tariff risk with 50% of footwear from Vietnam (facing 46% tariff) and significant China exposure (54% tariff). UBS upgraded Nucor and Steel Dynamics on March 24 on tariff protection for domestic steel. UnitedHealth benefiting from CMS Medicare Advantage payment increase exceeding 5% and near-total tariff insulation. No major earnings this week — positioning around Liberation Day is the dominant activity.

sections.title: TechAI
sections.content: Apple is the most exposed mega-cap with 90% of iPhones produced in China (facing 54% total tariff). Morgan Stanley estimates 17-18% price increases needed across all Apple products. Apple's India/Vietnam diversification strategy fails as those countries also face high tariffs (26% and 46% respectively). Nvidia held GTC 2025 in March showcasing Blackwell GPU transition — semiconductor stocks relatively resilient due to initial tariff exemptions for chips, but Trump threatening semiconductor tariffs 'very soon.' TSMC committed $100B US investment in March WH meeting. Palantir tariff-resistant as software-based but faces DOGE spending cut risk on government contracts.

sections.title: Energy
sections.content: Gold hit all-time record $3,122.80 per troy ounce on March 31, having surged past $3,000 for the first time on March 14 — on track for strongest quarter since 1986. WTI crude oil around $69-71/bbl in late March — moderate but facing demand destruction risk from global trade war slowdown. OPEC output decisions adding uncertainty. Steel futures rose to $945 on domestic demand from 25% tariff protection. Industrial metals face demand headwinds from global slowdown fears. Gold ETF inflows surging — biggest weekly inflow since March 2022.

sections.title: Policy
sections.content: Liberation Day Executive Orders will invoke IEEPA (International Emergency Economic Powers Act) declaring national emergency over the US trade deficit — unprecedented authority for tariffs. Pharmaceutical products initially exempt from reciprocal tariffs, providing tailwind for pharma/healthcare. Semiconductor tariffs threatened 'very soon' by Trump. DOGE spending cuts creating political headwinds for government contractors. CMS announced 5%+ Medicare Advantage payment increase for 2026, significantly exceeding expectations and boosting managed care. European defense spending unlocked by Germany's constitutional amendment and EU's ReArm Europe plan.

recommendations.thesis: Information asymmetry is the edge here. The market expects China tariffs but the Vietnam rate (46%) is the surprise that specifically destroys Nike's manufacturing strategy. Nike spent years shifting from China to Vietnam as a hedge, and that hedge just imploded. With 50% of footwear from Vietnam and 28% of apparel, this is existential margin pressure. Nike already struggling with brand challenges — tariffs compound every problem simultaneously. The 11% premarket drop after the announcement confirms thesis direction.
recommendations.catalyst: Nike is the single most exposed large-cap to Liberation Day tariffs. 50% of footwear from Vietnam (46% tariff), significant China exposure (54% tariff). The Vietnam pivot — Nike's core risk mitigation strategy built over years — is completely destroyed by these rates. Market does not yet price in the severity of Vietnam-specific tariffs at 46%. $1.5B cost increase estimate may be conservative given scope. Stock will gap down hard on April 2-3 as the full implications sink in.

recommendations.thesis: Gold is the ultimate Liberation Day trade. The metal is already at records but the April 2 announcement will trigger a new wave of safe-haven buying as markets realize the tariff scope exceeds all expectations. Newmont provides leveraged exposure to gold prices — operating margins expand disproportionately with each dollar increase in gold. The company's record FCF and buyback provide fundamental floor even if gold consolidates. Gold ETF inflows at highest since March 2022 confirm institutional positioning.
recommendations.catalyst: Gold at all-time highs above $3,100 heading into the most aggressive tariff announcement in modern history. Safe-haven demand will intensify post-Liberation Day as investors realize tariffs are far more severe than expected. Newmont is the world's largest gold miner with record margins, expanding free cash flow, and a $6B buyback program providing EPS support.

recommendations.thesis: Apple's China concentration is well-known but the market hasn't grasped that the diversification strategy (India, Vietnam) is equally doomed under these tariffs. Every single Apple manufacturing country faces 20%+ tariffs. The pricing impact is catastrophic for consumer demand — a $1,599 iPhone Pro Max could reach $2,300. Apple cannot absorb this without destroying margins. The stock's 9% single-day drop and 23% four-day decline validates the magnitude of the thesis.
recommendations.catalyst: Apple is the defining stock story of Liberation Day. 90% of iPhones manufactured in China facing 54% cumulative tariff. Every alternative production country (India 26%, Vietnam 46%, Thailand) also faces punitive tariffs — there is no escape route. Morgan Stanley estimates 17-18% price increases needed across all product lines. iPhone could jump from $799 to $1,142 at the low end. $770B in market cap erased in 4 days post-announcement confirms the severity.

recommendations.thesis: Nucor is the cleanest long trade in the tariff theme. Unlike defensive plays that merely avoid tariff damage, Nucor actively benefits from tariffs — every imported ton replaced by domestic steel flows directly to Nucor's top and bottom line. The UBS upgrade provides institutional validation. Steel futures at $945 confirm pricing power. The Liberation Day announcement will only strengthen this thesis as the breadth of tariffs becomes clear and more import substitution accelerates.
recommendations.catalyst: Direct tariff beneficiary with fresh UBS upgrade to buy (March 24, PT $160 vs ~$127 stock price — 26% upside to target). 25% steel tariffs with NO exemptions already in effect since March 4. Steel futures at $945 and rising as buyers replace lost imports. Domestic EAF production means zero import cost exposure. Liberation Day will further reinforce tariff narrative and drive institutional buying into domestic producers.

recommendations.thesis: The auto tariff thesis has a hard catalyst date (April 3 implementation) that creates urgency. GM's specific exposure metrics make it the worst-positioned major automaker — the 48% import rate combined with sub-40% domestic parts content creates a double hit that competitors don't face to the same degree. Bernstein's 79% EBIT decline estimate is institutional-grade analysis that fund managers will anchor to. The March 26 drop was just the opening act; actual implementation creates forced selling as supply chain costs become real.
recommendations.catalyst: 25% auto tariffs effective April 3 — two days away. GM has the highest tariff exposure among all automakers: 80% North America revenue concentration, 48% vehicle import rate, and less than 40% US parts content in domestic builds. Bernstein's analysis is devastating: 79% EBIT decline, 81% EPS decline, and $4.1B free cash flow destruction. Already dropped 7% on the March 26 announcement but the actual tariff implementation starting April 3 will compound the pain.

recommendations.thesis: UNH offers the rare combination of defensive positioning (zero tariff exposure, non-cyclical demand) AND an active positive catalyst (Medicare Advantage payment increase). Most defensive plays merely avoid damage — UNH has a genuine earnings catalyst. The stock rose 7% on April 9 when the full tariff scope became clear, confirming institutional rotation into healthcare as a tariff shelter. In a market where correlation goes to 1 during panic selling, healthcare's explicit tariff exemption makes it the last sector standing.
recommendations.catalyst: Double defensive play combining tariff immunity with a positive catalyst. Nearly 100% domestic revenue in healthcare services means zero tariff exposure. CMS Medicare Advantage payment increase exceeding 5% provides earnings tailwind that competitors won't match. Healthcare explicitly exempt from reciprocal tariffs. In a market about to be rocked by the worst tariff announcement since 1930, UNH is the ultimate institutional shelter.
